category.name: Close Work, Settle Cost and Update Records

derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Every field traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body per _Collab/SOURCE_AUTHORITY_PACK.md section D-ter. Nothing is generalised from a client programme or a product.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: THE BOUNDARY THIS CATEGORY SITS ON. The work and field systems hold the asset from an OPERATIONS standpoint and do not perform its financial aspects. What crosses is work order actuals for labour and material, which units of property were added and removed, and the in-service date. Everything else - accumulating and clearing construction work in progress, the allowance for funds used during construction, distributing settled cost across units, depreciation and retirement - happens in a property accounting system this discipline does not own. A process accruing the construction allowance was written into 5.2 and withdrawn once that boundary was stated.

IEC 61968-6 cl. 4.2 has no component for property or plant accounting. Sixteen codes and none is the plant record, so the property system is placed on FIN and the absence is recorded rather than filled with an invented code. The consequence is real: 5.3.2 and 5.3.3 describe an exchange with a separate system of record and the vocabulary cannot name the far end of it.

A compatible unit and a unit of property are different objects sharing a word. The compatible unit is an estimating and design construct held in the work system, carrying the account assignment; the unit of property is what the accounts capitalise and retire. They frequently correspond and are not the same object.

Used and useful was deliberately NOT modelled as a process. Plant enters rate base only where it is used and useful, and prudent investment has been struck from rate base on that ground, but the test is applied in a rate proceeding by a function that does not perform utility work. 5.3.5 records the in-service date and carries the test as a control; inventing a determination the work function does not make would be fabrication.

5.3.5 consumes the handover at 19.1.6 and does not perform it. The operational handover into service and the accounting in-service date are the same moment described by two functions; letting either drive the other silently is how an asset ends up in service on one record and under construction on the other.

What counts as ready for service is not stated by any source in the pack. The criteria are the operator's engineering judgment and belong per asset class rather than per job, so 5.3.5 states that they are recorded and does not state what they are.

The allowance for funds used during construction is computed on a formula the regulation prescribes, but its common equity rate is the rate granted in the last rate proceeding before the ratemaking body having primary jurisdiction. The reference cannot hold that number and does not.

The two halves of this category are prescribed to completely different depths. Cost settlement, capitalisation and unitisation are governed in detail by 18 CFR 101 and 18 CFR 125.3 - what may be charged, what a retirement unit is, how long each record is kept. The as-built and asset record half has almost nothing: 49 CFR 192.605(b)(3) requires construction records be AVAILABLE to operating personnel and says nothing about accuracy.

There is no federal as-built requirement for electric distribution at all. 16 U.S.C. 824o excludes local distribution from the bulk-power system and NESC ANSI/IEEE C2-2023 sets no record-keeping duty. Every as-built control in 5.4 is therefore gas-anchored, with the electric position stated as the operator's or a state's.

No federal standard sets positional accuracy for as-built records, gas or electric. ASCE 38-22 gives quality levels A to D as a defensible vocabulary, but the required level is not set by any standard.
No standard specifies the work order closure state model. Whether closure is one state or four, and what may reopen a closed order, is the operator's. 5.1.4 is marked judgment accordingly.

No standard specifies unitisation mechanics. 18 CFR 101 defines the retirement unit and requires additions and retirements to be recorded; how settled cost is distributed across units is an operator method. 5.3.2 is marked judgment accordingly.

The retention asymmetry is worth stating on its own: the continuing plant inventory ledger is kept 25 years under 18 CFR 125.3 Item 16(b), while the work order sheets behind it may be disposed of 5 years after clearance to plant account under Item 17. The property record outlives its own evidence by twenty years.
No standard specifies as-built acceptance criteria. 5.4.5 is marked judgment.
49 CFR 192.607 material verification and 192.709(a) permanent repair records are TRANSMISSION only. Distribution operators carry neither, which is the single most misquoted point in this category.

controls.text: Overhead may not be charged by adding an arbitrary percentage or amount to direct construction cost. It is allocated on a defined basis or not at all - the same rule that bound the estimate at 2.3.3.

The basis is evidentiary: payroll charged to construction overhead comes from time card distributions, or from periodic studies where that is impractical. Only overhead with a definite relation to construction may be capitalised. An estimate's loading at 2.2.3 is not that basis.
Settlement against an open work order that still has cost to come produces a false actual, and the variance against estimate is then measuring the settlement date rather than the work.

processes.name: Capture field redline against the issued design

group.name: Produce digital as-built and update asset records

processes.intent: Capture what was actually built, against the design that was issued.
activities: Take the design at the revision the work was released against
Record every departure from it as the crew found or made it
Capture the evidence that supports each departure
Return the redline against the work, not as a separate document

trigger.text: Work is complete and differs, or may differ, from the issued design.

inputs.what: Issued design at its released revision
Field observation of what was built

controls.text: For gas the operator must make construction records, maps and operating history available to appropriate operating personnel. Note what that requires and what it does not: availability, not accuracy.
A redline captured against the wrong design revision is worse than no redline. The revision released at 2.2.6 is the one it is captured against.

For electric distribution there is no federal as-built requirement at all. 16 U.S.C. 824o excludes local distribution and NESC sets no record-keeping duty, so the obligation is the operator's or a state's.

processes.name: Perform survey-grade asset location capture

group.name: Produce digital as-built and update asset records

processes.intent: Capture the position of what was installed to a stated accuracy.
activities: Determine the accuracy the asset class and its exposure require
Capture position while the asset is still exposed
Record the method and the accuracy actually achieved
Flag what could not be captured before cover

trigger.text: An asset is installed and its position must be captured before cover.

inputs.what: Required positional accuracy for the class
Survey control available at the site

outputs.what: Captured position with method and accuracy
Exception where position could not be captured

controls.text: Position is captured while the asset is exposed. After cover the only options are a records-based estimate or an excavation, and the first is what puts wrong positions into the map.

No federal standard sets positional accuracy for gas distribution or for electric. The quality levels in the subsurface utility engineering standard give a defensible vocabulary; the required level is the operator's or a state's to set.
The accuracy ACHIEVED is recorded, not only the accuracy required. A map that does not carry its own uncertainty gets trusted beyond it.

group.name: Produce digital as-built and update asset records

processes.intent: Record what was installed, what was removed and what was left abandoned.
activities: Record each unit installed with its identity and attributes
Record each unit removed and where it went
Record what was abandoned in place and why
Reconcile the three against the material issued at 5.2.2

trigger.text: An as-built redline requires its unit-level record.

outputs.what: Units installed with identity and attributes
Units abandoned in place with the reason

controls.text: Abandonment is not a records footnote. For gas it is governed in its own right and what is abandoned in place remains a thing the operator must know about, because the next excavation will find it.
Installed, removed and abandoned must reconcile with what was issued at 5.2.2. A difference is either material unaccounted for or an asset the record does not know about.
These units are what 5.3.2 unitises against. Taking them from the design rather than the field puts the wrong units in a record kept for twenty-five years.

group.name: Produce digital as-built and update asset records

processes.intent: Reconcile the as-built against the design and resolve what disagrees.
activities: Compare the as-built against the issued design revision
Classify each difference as recorded, resolvable or material
Return material differences to design for review
Record the reconciled position as the accepted as-built

trigger.text: An as-built record is complete and must be reconciled.

inputs.what: As-built record with units and positions
Issued design at its released revision

controls.text: A material difference is a design change discovered after the fact. It goes back through design review at 2.1.3, not into the record as though it were intended.
Reconciliation that resolves every difference in favour of the as-built hides the ones that should have prompted a design change. The classification is the control.

group.name: Produce digital as-built and update asset records

processes.intent: Have the as-built reviewed and accepted by someone accountable for it.
activities: Review the as-built against its evidence

trigger.text: A reconciled as-built is presented for acceptance.

inputs.what: Acceptance criteria for the asset class

controls.text: Acceptance is by a named person against stated criteria. An as-built that enters the record because nobody rejected it is the mechanism by which map quality decays.
The record accepted here is what 192.605(b)(3) makes available to operating personnel, and what the next crew will dig against.

processes.name: Update asset register and segmentation

group.name: Produce digital as-built and update asset records

processes.intent: Update the asset register and its segmentation from the accepted as-built.
activities: Create, amend or retire the asset records the work changed
Update attributes, class and criticality where they changed
Re-segment the linear asset where its measure basis changed
Apply the maintenance strategy to what is now in service

trigger.text: An as-built has been accepted and the register must follow it.

inputs.what: Existing register entries at the location
Maintenance strategy for the asset class

outputs.what: Maintenance strategy applied to new plant

controls.text: New plant with no maintenance strategy applied is new plant that generates no programmed work. The gap is silent until the first failure or the first audit.
Re-segmenting a linear asset moves the boundaries that condition, defect and work history are recorded against. History has to move with the boundary or it becomes unattributable.
For gas, the distribution integrity programme depends on knowledge of the system. The register updated here is that knowledge.

processes.name: Publish as-built change to the network model

group.name: Produce digital as-built and update asset records

processes.intent: Publish the change so the network model and everyone downstream sees it.
activities: Publish the asset and connectivity change to the network model
Confirm the spatial and non-spatial records agree
Notify the functions whose work depends on the change
Record the publication and resolve anything that rejected it

trigger.text: The asset register has been updated and the change must be published.

outputs.what: Rejection to resolve where the model would not accept it

controls.text: Network operations plans switching against the model. A model that does not carry a change made in the field is how a clearance gets issued against plant that is no longer there.
For gas, construction records and maps must be available to appropriate operating personnel. Publication is what makes them available rather than merely stored.
A rejected publication leaves the register and the model disagreeing. Rejections are resolved, not retried until they succeed.
